bull_bear.body:
- Stated continuous endeavour to maintain the taste and preferences of its customers while upgrading and developing new brands for both domestic and international markets
- Export-led growth: management notes that despite sluggish domestic demand from trade disruption and geo-political uncertainty, the Company achieved better results across markets, especially international
- Operates from a low-cost base country: the AR notes India has low production, farming and export cost versus other tobacco manufacturing countries, which management frames as an opportunity for Indian cigarette makers to extend and consolidate their international position
- Robust internal financial control commensurate with size, with an external and independent firm of Internal Auditors reporting directly to the Audit Committee; no reportable material weakness or significant deficiency was observed during or at the end of the year
- In-house research and development carried out using the existing manufacturing setup, with technology absorption efforts reported to have delivered product improvement and cost reduction
- Focus during the year on improving productivity, reducing costs and utilising cash flows most effectively
- Amiable industrial relations, with no strike or lockout reported that would have impacted operations (52 employees as on 31st March, 2026)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Punitive and unstable taxation on legal cigarettes — The MD&A names Taxation as a headline threat: cigarette tax rates in India are much higher than in China, the USA or the UK, and a key development in FY 2025-26 was the Government's massive increase in Excise duty plus the change in applicability of GST on MRP from February 1, 2026, which raised overall tax incidence and reinforced what the Company calls a long-standing unstable and discriminatory tax framework for legal cigarette manufacturers.
- Excise hikes are eroding the Company's core affordable 64 mm segment — Management states its main focus is the affordable 64 mm segment but that the continuous excise hike is making the Company's foothold weak in exactly that segment - a direct threat to the Company's chosen price point rather than a generic industry concern.
- Illegal cigarette trade and cheaper non-duty-paid product — The MD&A states that extremely high and constantly increasing tax rates provide a profitable opportunity for tax evasion through both internationally smuggled and domestic tax-evaded cigarettes, and that the availability of cheaper non-duty-paid cigarettes is impacting the Company's performance. The Tobacco Institute of India is cited as saying the high tax structure has itself created the market for smuggled foreign cigarettes.
- Extreme regulation of the product under COTPA — Tobacco control measures in India are described as the most stringent in the world, with the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003 (COTPA) as the principal comprehensive governing law - a permanent constraint on how the product can be made, sold and distributed.
- Mandated pictorial and text health warnings covering 85% of the pack — The Union Ministry of Health & Family Welfare mandates pictorial warnings on 85% of both the front and back panels, rotated every 12 months. The MD&A lists increased harsh pictorial warning among the factors impacting the Company's performance and, by consuming most of the pack face, it structurally limits branding and pack differentiation.
- Ban on advertising, promotion and sponsorship — Advertising through most forms of mass media is prohibited and there are restrictions on tobacco sponsorship and on publicising such sponsorship. This removes the normal route to building or defending a brand and works against the Company's own stated strategy of developing new brands, while campaigning by NGOs and forums against tobacco use and the passing of various smoking bans add to the pressure.
- Competition from larger players and, in the Board's own words, from established developers — The MD&A opens its risk section by saying the Company is exposed to stiff competition from other established developers in the market, and separately notes stiff competition from big players with regard to the marketing of new brands - a scale disadvantage for a company with 52 employees against national cigarette majors, and one that also reaches its real-estate subsidiaries.
- Concentration on a single product segment with an increasing dependence on exports amid sluggish domestic demand — The Company treats 'Manufacturing of Cigarette and Smoking Mixture' as its single primary business segment. Domestic demand continued to be sluggish throughout the year due to trade disruption and geo-political uncertainties, and the results the Company did achieve came especially from international markets, with export sales increasing to Rs. 5417.30 Lakhs from Rs. 2834.02 Lakhs against overall turnover of Rs. 10175.14 Lakhs - so a large and rising share of the business now rests on export markets and on foreign-exchange earnings.

outlook.body:
- Keep the affordable 64 mm cigarette segment as the Company's main product focus, even though continuous excise hikes are weakening its foothold there
- Regain the Company's lost place in the industry by improving its product portfolio and its technologies
- Maintain the taste and preferences of existing customers while upgrading and developing new brands for both domestic and international markets
- Improve productivity, reduce costs and utilise cash flows most effectively
- Conserve resources and plough the entire profit back into expansion activities rather than pay a dividend
- Grow the real-estate business through the wholly owned subsidiaries, with NTCIL Siliguri Estate Private Limited and NTCIL Realty Private Limited incorporated specifically to expand that business and tap newer opportunities
- Conserve energy through automation of the condenser tube cleaning system, of controls and sensors across manufacturing, air-conditioning and power generation, and of compressed air systems, plus continuous upgradation of machinery; and continue seeking alternate sources of energy to maintain the optimum combination of energies
- Carry out research and development in-house using the existing manufacturing setup rather than through separate material R&D spend
- Direct CSR primarily to programmes that promote education
- Enhance organisational capability through continuous learning and development and by nurturing distributed leadership so each business is managed by its own team of leaders
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Annual Report describes no cigarette-manufacturing capacity addition, no new line or plant and no commissioning timeline. The only expansion intent stated is financial and structural: the Board declared no dividend for FY2025-26 in order to meet growing funds requirements, conserve resources and plough the entire profit back into expansion activities, and made no transfer to Reserves. The named expansion vehicle is real estate rather than tobacco: as on 31st March, 2026 the Company had four wholly owned subsidiaries - NTCIL Infrastructure Private Limited, NTCIL Real Estate Private Limited, NTCIL Siliguri Estate Private Limited and NTCIL Realty Private Limited. Plans for securing growth in the real estate business through NTCIL Infrastructure and NTCIL Real Estate are stated to be under way with appropriate action to be taken at appropriate time for further development, while NTCIL Siliguri Estate and NTCIL Realty were incorporated with a view to expand the real estate business and tap newer opportunities and are yet to commence business operations. No company became or ceased to be a subsidiary, joint venture or associate during the year, and the Company has no joint venture or associate company. There has been no change in the nature of business, and no material changes or commitments affecting the financial position occurred between the year-end and the date of the report. On the manufacturing side the only capital-related activity described is incremental efficiency work - automation of the condenser tube cleaning system, of controls and sensors across manufacturing, air-conditioning and power generation, and of compressed air systems, plus continuous upgradation of machineries - with no timeline or capacity outcome attached.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Structural skew of Indian tobacco consumption: legal cigarettes are just 8% of total domestic tobacco consumption versus nearly 90% in most other countries, with 92% of Indian tobacco use in traditional and largely unregulated forms such as chewing tobacco, bidis, khaini and illicit cigarettes
- The Government of India's massive increase in Excise duty and the change in applicability of GST on MRP from February 1, 2026 raised overall tax incidence and reinforced the long-standing challenge of an unstable and discriminatory tax framework for legal cigarette manufacturers
- Domestic demand continued to be sluggish throughout the year due to trade disruption and geo-political uncertainties, while the Company managed to achieve better results across the different markets, especially international
- Continuous excise hikes are making the Company's foothold weak in its core affordable 64 mm segment
- Export opportunity: India has low production, farming and export cost compared with other tobacco manufacturing countries, and recent trends such as withdrawal/reduction of agricultural subsidy and escalating costing in the traditional cigarette exporting countries give the Indian cigarette industry significant opportunity to extend and consolidate its position in international markets
- Availability of cheaper non-duty-paid cigarettes and illegal trade (both internationally smuggled and domestic tax-evaded), fuelled by extremely high and constantly increasing tax rates, is impacting the Company's performance
- Stiff competition from big players with regard to the marketing of new brands
- Harsher pictorial and text health warnings covering 85 percent of the front and back panels and rotated every 12 months weigh on performance
- Margin commentary: interest coverage improved on higher profit helped by a decrease in raw material cost, while the operating profit margin declined due to an increase in operating costs
- Management's cautionary statement names raw material availability and prices, cyclical demand and pricing in the Company's principal markets, changes in government regulations and tax regimes, and economic developments in India as the important factors that could make actual results differ

risks.risk: Punitive and unstable taxation on legal cigarettes
risks.note: The MD&A names Taxation as a headline threat: cigarette tax rates in India are much higher than in China, the USA or the UK, and a key development in FY 2025-26 was the Government's massive increase in Excise duty plus the change in applicability of GST on MRP from February 1, 2026, which raised overall tax incidence and reinforced what the Company calls a long-standing unstable and discriminatory tax framework for legal cigarette manufacturers.

risks.risk: Excise hikes are eroding the Company's core affordable 64 mm segment
risks.note: Management states its main focus is the affordable 64 mm segment but that the continuous excise hike is making the Company's foothold weak in exactly that segment - a direct threat to the Company's chosen price point rather than a generic industry concern.

risks.risk: Illegal cigarette trade and cheaper non-duty-paid product
risks.note: The MD&A states that extremely high and constantly increasing tax rates provide a profitable opportunity for tax evasion through both internationally smuggled and domestic tax-evaded cigarettes, and that the availability of cheaper non-duty-paid cigarettes is impacting the Company's performance. The Tobacco Institute of India is cited as saying the high tax structure has itself created the market for smuggled foreign cigarettes.

risks.risk: Extreme regulation of the product under COTPA
risks.note: Tobacco control measures in India are described as the most stringent in the world, with the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003 (COTPA) as the principal comprehensive governing law - a permanent constraint on how the product can be made, sold and distributed.

risks.risk: Mandated pictorial and text health warnings covering 85% of the pack
risks.note: The Union Ministry of Health & Family Welfare mandates pictorial warnings on 85% of both the front and back panels, rotated every 12 months. The MD&A lists increased harsh pictorial warning among the factors impacting the Company's performance and, by consuming most of the pack face, it structurally limits branding and pack differentiation.

risks.risk: Ban on advertising, promotion and sponsorship
risks.note: Advertising through most forms of mass media is prohibited and there are restrictions on tobacco sponsorship and on publicising such sponsorship. This removes the normal route to building or defending a brand and works against the Company's own stated strategy of developing new brands, while campaigning by NGOs and forums against tobacco use and the passing of various smoking bans add to the pressure.

risks.risk: Competition from larger players and, in the Board's own words, from established developers
risks.note: The MD&A opens its risk section by saying the Company is exposed to stiff competition from other established developers in the market, and separately notes stiff competition from big players with regard to the marketing of new brands - a scale disadvantage for a company with 52 employees against national cigarette majors, and one that also reaches its real-estate subsidiaries.

risks.risk: Concentration on a single product segment with an increasing dependence on exports amid sluggish domestic demand
risks.note: The Company treats 'Manufacturing of Cigarette and Smoking Mixture' as its single primary business segment. Domestic demand continued to be sluggish throughout the year due to trade disruption and geo-political uncertainties, and the results the Company did achieve came especially from international markets, with export sales increasing to Rs. 5417.30 Lakhs from Rs. 2834.02 Lakhs against overall turnover of Rs. 10175.14 Lakhs - so a large and rising share of the business now rests on export markets and on foreign-exchange earnings.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: N T C Industries Limited is a Kolkata-headquartered manufacturer of cigarettes and smoking mixture whose main focus is the affordable 64 mm segment, with a rapidly growing export book and a real-estate arm held through wholly owned subsidiaries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company considers "Manufacturing of Cigarette and Smoking Mixture" as its primary business segment, and also earns revenue from the sale of FMCG products and from rental services. Its main focus is the affordable 64 mm cigarette segment, sold in the domestic market and increasingly exported, with the Company stating a continuous endeavour to maintain the taste and preferences of its customers while upgrading and developing new brands for both domestic and international markets. Separately, the Company pursues a real-estate business through four wholly owned subsidiaries, two of which are yet to commence operations.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural skew of Indian tobacco consumption: legal cigarettes are just 8% of total domestic tobacco consumption versus nearly 90% in most other countries, with 92% of Indian tobacco use in traditional and largely unregulated forms such as chewing tobacco, bidis, khaini and illicit cigarettes
- The Government of India's massive increase in Excise duty and the change in applicability of GST on MRP from February 1, 2026 raised overall tax incidence and reinforced the long-standing challenge of an unstable and discriminatory tax framework for legal cigarette manufacturers
- Domestic demand continued to be sluggish throughout the year due to trade disruption and geo-political uncertainties, while the Company managed to achieve better results across the different markets, especially international
- Continuous excise hikes are making the Company's foothold weak in its core affordable 64 mm segment
- Export opportunity: India has low production, farming and export cost compared with other tobacco manufacturing countries, and recent trends such as withdrawal/reduction of agricultural subsidy and escalating costing in the traditional cigarette exporting countries give the Indian cigarette industry significant opportunity to extend and consolidate its position in international markets
- Availability of cheaper non-duty-paid cigarettes and illegal trade (both internationally smuggled and domestic tax-evaded), fuelled by extremely high and constantly increasing tax rates, is impacting the Company's performance
- Stiff competition from big players with regard to the marketing of new brands
- Harsher pictorial and text health warnings covering 85 percent of the front and back panels and rotated every 12 months weigh on performance
- Margin commentary: interest coverage improved on higher profit helped by a decrease in raw material cost, while the operating profit margin declined due to an increase in operating costs
- Management's cautionary statement names raw material availability and prices, cyclical demand and pricing in the Company's principal markets, changes in government regulations and tax regimes, and economic developments in India as the important factors that could make actual results differ

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Keep the affordable 64 mm cigarette segment as the Company's main product focus, even though continuous excise hikes are weakening its foothold there
- Regain the Company's lost place in the industry by improving its product portfolio and its technologies
- Maintain the taste and preferences of existing customers while upgrading and developing new brands for both domestic and international markets
- Improve productivity, reduce costs and utilise cash flows most effectively
- Conserve resources and plough the entire profit back into expansion activities rather than pay a dividend
- Grow the real-estate business through the wholly owned subsidiaries, with NTCIL Siliguri Estate Private Limited and NTCIL Realty Private Limited incorporated specifically to expand that business and tap newer opportunities
- Conserve energy through automation of the condenser tube cleaning system, of controls and sensors across manufacturing, air-conditioning and power generation, and of compressed air systems, plus continuous upgradation of machinery; and continue seeking alternate sources of energy to maintain the optimum combination of energies
- Carry out research and development in-house using the existing manufacturing setup rather than through separate material R&D spend
- Direct CSR primarily to programmes that promote education
- Enhance organisational capability through continuous learning and development and by nurturing distributed leadership so each business is managed by its own team of leaders

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Annual Report describes no cigarette-manufacturing capacity addition, no new line or plant and no commissioning timeline. The only expansion intent stated is financial and structural: the Board declared no dividend for FY2025-26 in order to meet growing funds requirements, conserve resources and plough the entire profit back into expansion activities, and made no transfer to Reserves. The named expansion vehicle is real estate rather than tobacco: as on 31st March, 2026 the Company had four wholly owned subsidiaries - NTCIL Infrastructure Private Limited, NTCIL Real Estate Private Limited, NTCIL Siliguri Estate Private Limited and NTCIL Realty Private Limited. Plans for securing growth in the real estate business through NTCIL Infrastructure and NTCIL Real Estate are stated to be under way with appropriate action to be taken at appropriate time for further development, while NTCIL Siliguri Estate and NTCIL Realty were incorporated with a view to expand the real estate business and tap newer opportunities and are yet to commence business operations. No company became or ceased to be a subsidiary, joint venture or associate during the year, and the Company has no joint venture or associate company. There has been no change in the nature of business, and no material changes or commitments affecting the financial position occurred between the year-end and the date of the report. On the manufacturing side the only capital-related activity described is incremental efficiency work - automation of the condenser tube cleaning system, of controls and sensors across manufacturing, air-conditioning and power generation, and of compressed air systems, plus continuous upgradation of machineries - with no timeline or capacity outcome attached.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Stated continuous endeavour to maintain the taste and preferences of its customers while upgrading and developing new brands for both domestic and international markets
- Export-led growth: management notes that despite sluggish domestic demand from trade disruption and geo-political uncertainty, the Company achieved better results across markets, especially international
- Operates from a low-cost base country: the AR notes India has low production, farming and export cost versus other tobacco manufacturing countries, which management frames as an opportunity for Indian cigarette makers to extend and consolidate their international position
- Robust internal financial control commensurate with size, with an external and independent firm of Internal Auditors reporting directly to the Audit Committee; no reportable material weakness or significant deficiency was observed during or at the end of the year
- In-house research and development carried out using the existing manufacturing setup, with technology absorption efforts reported to have delivered product improvement and cost reduction
- Focus during the year on improving productivity, reducing costs and utilising cash flows most effectively
- Amiable industrial relations, with no strike or lockout reported that would have impacted operations (52 employees as on 31st March, 2026)
